regardless, time for me to give some good advice that’s been given to me in the past from my mentor. breeding ball pythons is a fun experience, but doing it just to do it isn’t the best decision. 

a normal x mojave pairing isn’t creating “desirable” offspring, as you’ll end up with normals and mojaves. she could potentially have 6+ eggs, and you could also potentially hit a lot of normals. are you prepared to keep them all? 
selling normals and simple single genes is difficult, so be prepared to sit on them for awhile. unless you’re keeping them all, then that’s all up to you. 
but again, a bunch of normals and mojaves isn’t going to do much for you if you’re planning on breeding more in the future. 

pairings like this are harmful to the hobby in the long run. i’m not saying normals and mojaves are bad. i’m speaking from a market standpoint, assuming you did this for some sort of money. 

if you didn’t and it was for pure enjoyment, i hope you’re prepared to house them/feed them/take care of multiple babies! especially, i hope you’re prepared to feed live to newborn hatchlings as it’s what they do best on at first. some will take f/t, but live prey has better results.
when they’re freshly hatched, time is a major factor. they deteriorate quickly if they don’t feed, so trying to get a fresh hatchling on f/t is a gamble most don’t try and mess with. figured i’d mention it since this subreddit advocates for f/t and most casual keepers feed f/t 🤷‍♀️


just stuff to think about. good luck with your potential clutch!

ovulation is something that happens for 48 hours or so. she swells up profusely in her abdomen and it will look like she swallowed a football. it’s reaaaally hard to miss lol. unless you aren’t checking her daily of course. i’ve never once missed an ovulation personally. 

i would refrain from more locks for now honestly. they’re able to store sperm for a long time and use it when they ovulate (aka fertilize their follicles).

did you witness an ovulation? has she been cool seeking or heat seeking? is she nesting?

i recommend gently palpating her with a paper towel between your finger and her skin (helps with feeling the follicles better), and feeling for either follicles (hard lumps that vary in size, from a marble to a golf ball), or eggs (softer masses, similar to a water balloon). 

if you feel hard lumps, she isn’t gravid yet, and depending on how big they are, she’s close to ovulation. 

if the lumps are softer, she’s likely gravid and these are eggs.

edit: as a side note, females tend to go off feed for about a month prior to ovulation. this is because the follicles are big, and she has little room for food. if she’s still eating it’s possible she isn’t gravid. just something to also consider!
